body: I have traced back the issue to the [`Thresholds.Run` method](https://github.com/grafana/k6/blob/master/metrics/thresholds.go#L191). As I debug through the execution of this script's execution, the `ts.sinked["med"]` value remains `0`.

I think this might be happening because we are not calling the `TrendSink`'s `Calc()` method, which is the thing that actually calculates and updates the value of `Med`: https://github.com/grafana/k6/blob/11deb073b9dd628f68b8c00aa7cc4de427955694/metrics/sink.go#L123-L137

Or at least I don't see where we are calling it in `Thresholds.Run()`, while it internally is called by both the percentile and the format methods:
https://github.com/grafana/k6/blob/11deb073b9dd628f68b8c00aa7cc4de427955694/metrics/sink.go#L139-L140
https://github.com/grafana/k6/blob/11deb073b9dd628f68b8c00aa7cc4de427955694/metrics/sink.go#L103-L114

And if there is a threshold on `med` for a `Trend` metric without a percentile threshold on the same metric to call `Calc()` eventually, the value of `Med` will never actually be calculated: https://github.com/grafana/k6/blob/11deb073b9dd628f68b8c00aa7cc4de427955694/metrics/thresholds.go#L191-L202

I might be missing something, but I think this is at least part of the problem. An easy workaround would be to just use `p(50)` instead of `med`, since they are basically the same thing, but this feels like a major bug :disappointed: Potentially enough for releasing v0.41.1 :thinking:

Here is a simpler script that demonstrates the issue:
```js
import { Trend } from 'k6/metrics';

export let options = {
    scenarios: {
        issueHappensWithCoreTrendMetric: {
            executor: 'constant-arrival-rate',
            rate: 1,
            duration: '10s',
            preAllocatedVUs: 2,
        },
    },
    thresholds: {
        custom_trend: [{
            threshold: 'med<39',
            abortOnFail: true
        }],
    },
};

const customTrend = new Trend('custom_trend');

export default function () {
    customTrend.add(80);
}
```

If you run it with `--verbose`, you'd see something like this:
```
...
DEBU[0002] running thresholds                            component=metrics-engine metric_name=custom_trend
DEBU[0004] running thresholds                            component=metrics-engine metric_name=custom_trend
DEBU[0006] running thresholds                            component=metrics-engine metric_name=custom_trend
DEBU[0008] running thresholds                            component=metrics-engine metric_name=custom_trend
DEBU[0010] running thresholds                            component=metrics-engine metric_name=custom_trend
...
DEBU[0010] Processing metrics and thresholds after the test run has ended...  component=engine
...
DEBU[0010] running thresholds                            component=metrics-engine metric_name=custom_trend
DEBU[0010] Engine run terminated cleanly                
...
DEBU[0010] Engine: Thresholds terminated                 component=engine
...

   ✓ custom_trend.........: avg=80      min=80      med=80      max=80      p(90)=80      p(95)=80     
     data_received........: 0 B 0 B/s
     data_sent............: 0 B 0 B/s
     iteration_duration...: avg=40.28µs min=31.58µs med=37.69µs max=63.47µs p(90)=62.05µs p(95)=62.76µs
     iterations...........: 11  1.099916/s
     vus..................: 2   min=2      max=2
     vus_max..............: 2   min=2      max=2

DEBU[0010] Waiting for engine processes to finish...    
DEBU[0010] Metrics processing winding down...            component=engine
DEBU[0010] running thresholds                            component=metrics-engine metric_name=custom_trend
DEBU[0010] Thresholds failed                             component=metrics-engine metric_name=custom_trend
DEBU[0010] Everything has finished, exiting k6!         
DEBU[0010] Stopping 1 outputs...                         component=output-manager
DEBU[0010] Stopping...                                   component=metrics-engine-ingester
DEBU[0010] Stopped!                                      component=metrics-engine-ingester
ERRO[0010] some thresholds have failed                  
exit status 99
```

The threshold has always been breached, and k6 was supposed to abort the script immediately when it noticed. However, it was happily running it until the end, as if the threshold was seemingly not being crossed. However, after the summary was generated, which required calculation of percentiles and thus the calling of `TrendSink.Calc()`, the next time the thresholds were calculated, k6 realized the `med` threshold was crossed and exited the test with the right exit code.

This bug seems to have been introduced in k6 v0.37.0, probably due to the [threshold refactoring there](https://github.com/grafana/k6/blob/master/release%20notes/v0.37.0.md#introduced-stricter-thresholds-parsing-2400). 

And, for anyone that has hit it, the workaround is to just replace `med` with `p(50)` in your threshold definitions. They are the same thing, after all, `med` is just there for convenience.
Heads up, I've started working on a fix for this 👋🏻

issue.title: Fix 2755 and ensure evaulation of thresholds over trend metrics median

repository.name: k6
repository.description: A modern load testing tool, using Go and JavaScript

license.name: GNU Affero General Public License v3.0

issue.body:
This PR addresses #2755. 

Turns out the Trend Sink median value was never calculated in time for thresholds to be able to evaluate them. The reason for that is that the median value can be quite expensive to compute, as it relies most notably on sorting the sink's array of values. As a result, its calculation happens in a dedicated `Calc` method. It appears we forgot to call that method in the `Thresholds.Run` method during our latest refactoring of the thresholds system.

This PR ensures the `Calc` method is called just in time, so that the costly computation only happens when Thresholds are effectively evaluated. It also adds a couple of tests to protect us from regressions in the future. Finally, it adds some documentation and comments to the code, so that next time we touch that part of the code, there is some background information available to the contributor.

Thanks a lot to @imiric for his collaboration in tracking and getting this issue resolved 🙇🏻 🎉 

Let me know what you think 👍🏻

issue.title: Either renaming or dropping the `Sink.Calc` method

repository.name: k6
repository.description: A modern load testing tool, using Go and JavaScript

license.name: GNU Affero General Public License v3.0

issue.body:
### Feature Description

In the context of #2755 [resolution](https://github.com/grafana/k6/pull/2759), we have found out with @imiric that the `TrendSink.Calc` method is only implemented for the `TrendSink`. Furthermore, although it is named `Calc`, its actual job is to compute the median value of the sink.


### Suggested Solution (optional)

We would like to propose some ideas on how to improve that state in the future by either:
- dropping that method from the interface itself to only keep its implementation on the `TrendSink`
- converting that method in a dedicated helper function and let whoever relies on the median value to call it on the `TrendSink.Values`
- renaming that method to `Median` or something along those lines (in line with the `P` method), for consistency, and to explicit what it's used for.

### Already existing or connected issues / PRs (optional)

#2755 
#2759 
#2320
